question: What is my purpose as a man?
seo_title: What Is My Purpose as a Man? A Biblical Answer | TheWrkShop
description: God almost never starts with what you don't have. He starts with what's already in your hand. How to find your purpose, from Exodus 4:2.
answer: Your purpose isn't something you have to invent or find at the end of a long search. God almost never starts with what you don't have; He starts with what's already in your hand. Your purpose is to know God and become like Christ, and then to put what He's already given you, your gifts, your story, even your scars, to work for the people He's placed in front of you.

sections.heading: "What is that in your hand?"
paragraphs: When God called Moses, Moses gave Him every reason he wasn't enough: not eloquent, not credible, not the right man. God didn't argue. He asked, "What is that in your hand?" A staff. An ordinary shepherd's tool. God used it to part the sea.

The pattern repeats all through Scripture. To the widow about to lose her sons, Elisha asked, "What do you have in your house?" A small jar of oil. When the crowd was hungry, Jesus asked, "How many loaves do you have?" Five loaves and two fish. Each time the person thought, "It's not enough." Each time, God started there.

sections.heading: The human pattern vs. God's pattern
paragraphs: The human pattern says, "I don't have enough." God's pattern asks, "What do you have?" That question exposes scarcity thinking, uncovers resources you've overlooked, confronts fear and invites partnership. The miracle is often hidden inside the thing people dismissed.

sections.heading: Purpose is who you're becoming, then what you do
paragraphs: Ephesians 2:10 says you are God's handiwork, created for good works He prepared in advance. Notice the order: first His work in you, then His work through you. Purpose isn't a title or a job. It's faithfulness with what's in your hand, in the place you are, for the people in front of you.
Most men are waiting for a bigger assignment. God is usually asking about the one they already have.

scriptures.text: Then the LORD said to him, “What is that in your hand?” “A staff,” he replied.
For we are God’s handiwork, created in Christ Jesus to do good works, which God prepared in advance for us to do.
Each of you should use whatever gift you have received to serve others, as faithful stewards of God’s grace in its various forms.
Elisha replied to her, “How can I help you? Tell me, what do you have in your house?” “Your servant has nothing there at all,” she said, “except a small jar of olive oil.”

steps: Take the private [What's in Your Hand?](/tools/whats-in-your-hand/) inventory: your skills, resources, story, scars, relationships and the hard things you've survived.
Circle the one you've been dismissing as "not enough." Ask God what He might want to do with it.
Take the free [Spiritual Gifts Assessment](/assessment.html) to see how God has wired you to serve.
This week, use one thing on your list to serve one person, without being asked and without telling anyone.

tool.title: What's in Your Hand? A Private Purpose Inventory
tool.text: See what God has already put in your hands, name the excuse you've been using, and take one step this week. About 10 minutes. Nothing is saved or sent.

faqs.q: How do I know what God is calling me to do?
faqs.a: Start with what's already clear: love God, love people, and be faithful where you are. Then look at what's in your hand and the needs in front of you. Calling usually becomes clearer through obedience, not before it.

faqs.q: What if I feel like I've wasted years?
faqs.a: God wastes nothing that's surrendered to Him. Moses spent forty years tending sheep before God used that staff. Your past, including your failures, can become part of what's in your hand.
Your job can be a big part of how you live out your purpose, but it isn't the whole of it. Your purpose goes with you into every role: husband, father, friend, worker and brother.
